title: Finance & Legal Integrated Playbook: Budgeting, Contracts, Procurement, Revenue Recognition & Billing (Q5 2026)
author: Ava Martinez
content:
Overview:
This integrated playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's standard processes and controls for annual budgeting and rolling forecasts, procurement and contract approvals, vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition & billing. The objective is to ensure consistent financial governance, reduce cycle time for purchases and contracts, and align revenue recognition to contractual delivery under ASC 606 principles. This document is intended for finance, legal, procurement partners, product and engineering managers, and people who sign contracts or approve spend.

Scope:
- Applies to all Redwood legal entities and operating units (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) unless a contract or local policy explicitly supersedes.
- Covers: annual budgeting, monthly/quarterly forecasting cadence, procurement thresholds & approvals, purchase order (PO) creation, contract lifecycle (negotiation to signature), vendor onboarding, and revenue recognition and billing treatment for standard customer arrangements.

Definitions:
- PO: Purchase Order
- RevRec: Revenue Recognition
- Deferred revenue: cash received for performance obligations not yet satisfied
- Contract owner: Redwood employee responsible for contract terms and commercial relationship

Key owners and contacts:
- Finance (Budgeting & Forecasting): Emma Brooks (emma.brooks@redwood.com)
- Procurement & Vendor Mgmt: Marcus Lee (marcus.lee@redwood.com)
- Legal (Contracts): Priya Kapoor (priya.kapoor@redwood.com)
- Billing & AR: Liam Chen (liam.chen@redwood.com)
- Escalation (Finance Director): Nora Patel (nora.patel@redwood.com)

1) Annual Budgeting & Rolling Forecasts
- Calendar and deliverables (annual cycle):
  1. Budget kickoff (mid-Oct): CFO distributes targets and guidance for next fiscal year.
  2. Department submissions (end-Nov): functional budgets due in Workday/Anaplan.
  3. Cross-functional review (Dec): finance runs consolidation, senior leadership reviews.
  4. Final approval (by 1st week of Jan): CEO/CFO approve and publish budgets.
- Rolling forecast cadence: monthly 12-month rolling forecast with quarterly deep-dive.
- Assumptions and scenarios: provide base, upside, downside scenarios; modeling for headcount, cloud/inference costs, sales bookings, churn, and gross margin.
- Ownership: Finance owns consolidation; product & engineering provide capacity and cost drivers (GPU hours, model serving costs).
- Required artifacts: budget workbook, headcount plan, capex requests, variance commentary.

Budget approval thresholds (examples):
- Up to $25k: Department head approval
- $25k - $250k: Finance manager + Department head
- $250k - $1M: VP Finance + Department head
- > $1M: CFO + CEO (board notification for > $5M strategic commitments)

2) Procurement & Vendor Onboarding
- Procurement channels: preferred vendors listed in Vendor Registry. Use Procurement Portal (ServiceNow) for POs and vendor requests.
- Standard process (high level):
  1. Requestor creates procurement request with justification, budget code, and estimated cost.
  2. Procurement reviews vendor, checks preferred status, and requests vendor W-9/Company registration.
  3. For new vendors, Legal/Procurement run minimal risk assessment and require standard vendor agreement unless redlines are flagged.
  4. PO issued following approvals and once contract (if required) is executed.
- Vendor onboarding checklist:
  - Completed vendor profile in Procurement Portal
  - W-9 or equivalent tax docs
  - Insurance certificate (if required by threshold)
  - Security questionnaire or SOC2 report (if vendor will access customer data or infra)
  - Payment terms and remittance instructions

Procurement approval matrix (detailed):
| Estimated Annual Spend | Approval Required | Contract Review | PO Required |
|------------------------|-------------------|-----------------|------------|
| <$25k                 | Department head   | Standard T&Cs   | Optional   |
| $25k - $250k          | Finance manager + Dept head | Legal review if custom clauses | Yes |
| $250k - $1M           | VP Finance + Dept head | Legal review required | Yes |
| >$1M                  | CFO + CEO         | Legal & Exec review; commercial terms committee | Yes |

Procurement red flags (escalate to Legal/Procurement):
- Vendor asks to use non-standard indemnity or IP assignment terms
- Vendor requires broad data access without SOC2 or equivalent controls
- Payment in crypto or offshore-only remittance with limited documentation

3) Contract Lifecycle & Standard Contracting Principles
- Contract owner: assigned at negotiation start. Owner responsibilities: stakeholder alignment, tracking deadlines, coordinating signatures, and retaining executed contract in Contract Repository (DocuSign + Contract Lifecycle Management (CLM) system).
- Standard templates: Master Services Agreement (MSA), Statement of Work (SOW), Order Form, Data Processing Agreement (DPA), Confidentiality Agreement (NDA). Use the most recent templates in CLM.
- Negotiation guardrails (Legal):
  - Do not agree to open-ended liability beyond $5M without Legal/Exec approval.
  - Standard payment terms: Net 30 unless Finance approves Net 45/60 for strategic customers.
  - Data residency and security controls: require appropriate DPA; for regulated customers, route to Private deployment / on-prem options.
- Signature authorities:
  - Up to $250k contract value: VP Sales / VP Product (contract-specific delegation)
  - $250k - $1M: CFO sign-off required
  - > $1M: CEO sign-off required (legal to coordinate board notice if material)

Contract execution steps (numbered checklist):
1. Draft SOW/Order Form and select applicable MSA template.
2. Run commercial review: pricing, payment terms, termination rights.
3. Legal review: redlines, IP, indemnity, data clauses.
4. Finalize and route for signatures via DocuSign.
5. Procurement creates PO (if applicable) and links to contract.
6. Store executed contract in CLM and update Contract Registry with key metadata (counterparty, start/end dates, renewal terms, owner, revenue treatment).

4) Revenue Recognition & Billing (RevRec)
Principles and policy summary:
- Redwood recognizes revenue according to the performance obligations in customer contracts under ASC 606 principles: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price to obligations, recognize when/ as obligations are satisfied.
- Common customer arrangements: usage-based hosted API (metered per-token/embedding), committed monthly/annual Dedicated capacity (capacity reservation), Private deployment (license + support + professional services), professional services (implementation).

Revenue treatment guideline (by product):
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize as usage occurs (variable consideration). Bill monthly in arrears with supporting usage report. Estimate and constrain variable consideration based on historical collection and reversal rates.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): If committed monthly/annual fee grants access to capacity over time, recognize ratably over the commitment term. If there are deliverables (migration, onboarding), separate (and defer) revenue for PS until delivered.
- Private deployment (license + support): Distinct license vs support obligations should be evaluated. For perpetual license components recognized on delivery if control transfers; support and updates recognized ratably over the support term. For subscription licenses, recognize ratably over term.
- Professional services: Recognize based on completion of milestones or percentage of completion when objective measures exist; otherwise, on acceptance.

Invoicing and billing cycles:
- Standard customer billing: Net 30; invoices issued monthly for recurring and monthly usage unless otherwise negotiated.
- Prepaid arrangements: cash received in advance is recorded as deferred revenue and recognized over the service period.
- Credit memos & adjustments: process via AR with reference to original invoice; approvals for credits > $5k require Finance manager approval.

Sample journal entries (illustrative):
- Invoice for prepaid annual subscription (cash received):
  Dr Cash 100,000
  Cr Deferred revenue 100,000
- Monthly recognition for 12-month term:
  Dr Deferred revenue 8,333
  Cr Revenue 8,333
- Usage-based invoice recognized at billing (after usage month):
  Dr Accounts receivable 5,000
  Cr Revenue 5,000

Revenue cut-off controls and month-end close:
- Usage data and billing batch must be reconciled by Billing & AR before close. Reconciliations to include: usage totals vs billing system, deferred revenue aging, subscription scheduling.
- Close checklist items: reconcile AR subledger to GL, unbilled receivables review, revenue variance analysis, and obtain sign-off from Billing owner (Liam Chen).

5) Billing Exceptions, Collections, and Disputes
- Dispute handling: customer must submit dispute within 30 days of invoice. Disputed amounts are not written off automatically; record a billing dispute ticket in Billing system and hold collections until resolution for the disputed amount.
- Collections cadence: 30/60/90 day aging reminders; escalate to Sales and Legal for amounts > 90 days. For delinquent accounts > 120 days, consider hold of service per contract and pursue collections/legal remediation.
- Write-off approvals: write-offs > $10k require VP Finance sign-off.

6) Controls, Reporting & KPIs
- Key reports maintained monthly: booked ARR, recognized revenue, deferred revenue schedule, DSO, churn by ARR, bookings vs. billings, unbilled backlog.
- Controls: separation of duties between Contract Owners, Revenue/ Billing, and GL posting. All significant contracts (> $250k) must have contract metadata entered in CLM and revenue treatment approved by Finance before first billing.
- Internal audit readiness: retain supporting docs for revenue recognition decisions, usage extracts, contract terms, and pricing schedules for a minimum of 7 years.

7) Exceptions & Escalation Paths
- Non-standard contract clauses: escalate to Legal with documented business justification and an approved risk acceptance form.
- Accelerated recognition requests or carve-outs: require VP Finance + Accounting sign-off and documentation of the rationale and accounting treatment.
- Procurement exceptions to preferred vendor list: Procurement + Finance must approve and document exception in the Procurement Portal.

Appendices:
A. Templates & Links:
- Contract templates (MSA, SOW, DPA, NDA): stored in CLM link: /clm/templates
- Procurement Portal (ServiceNow): /tools/procurement

B. Sample journal entry mapping (GL codes):
- 4000 Revenue - Hosted API
- 4010 Revenue - Dedicated
- 4020 Revenue - Professional Services
- 2300 Deferred Revenue
- 1200 Accounts Receivable

C. Frequently asked questions:
Q: How do we treat trial credits and free tiers?
A: Track trial credits separately in Billing system; no revenue recognized until billed or converted to paid usage. Large strategic trials with contract commitments should be routed to Legal + Finance for special handling.

Document governance:
- Owner: Finance (Emma Brooks) with Legal (Priya Kapoor) as co-owner for contracting rules.
- Review cadence: Annual full policy review and ad-hoc updates for material accounting standard changes or material process changes.
- Change log: maintain a brief change log in CLM for major policy updates.

For questions or to request an exception, contact finance-legal@redwood.com or open a ticket in the Procurement Portal.
